feature: Ask's redlines on screens unlike the settings pane
summary: Ask now measures a glowing gradient button, a dark inspector panel and one named card instead of measuring the wrong thing or nothing. Asked how big a button is and how far it sits under a paragraph, it lays exactly those two.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default.

try.do: Open a screenshot of a web page with one big call-to-action button (Tests/PhotonzRenderTests/Fixtures/download-pill-2x.png works).
try.shotNote: Drawn by the eval's own render of the document, not a window capture.

try.do: Press Ask and type: how big is the download button, and how far is it from the paragraph above it?
Open a screenshot of a dark inspector panel and ask: spec the spacing in this panel.
try.shotNote: Drawn by the eval's own render of the document, not a window capture.

try.do: Open a screenshot with a card in it and ask: measure the padding inside the meeting card.
try.shotNote: Drawn by the eval's own render of the document, not a window capture.

try.do: Command Z once and check every mark goes in one step.

evaluate: On the button, are the size and the space above it the two numbers you would have written by hand?
On the dark panel, do the row height and the space above the dropdown read as the spacing that matters?
On the card, does Ask measure the card's own padding, or still something nearby?
rough: No mock covers Ask's redline output; it is judged against the eval's rubric.
Readouts still say px on a 2x picture and can land far from their lines on a dense panel (a-redline-of-a-2x-screenshot-reads-in-points-wit).
A small line of words inside a button's glow is not seen, so a readout can sit on it (the version line under the download button).
On the named card the model still lays some calipers of its own in odd places; the card case scores 27.9 against 77 for the button.
